text: The researchers extracted clove buds with 80% methanol, concentrated the extract and freeze-dried it before encapsulation.[1] They prepared six wall-material blends of maltodextrin (MD, dextrose equivalent 16.5–19.5) and gum arabic (GA), mixed freeze-dried extract with a 30% w/v wall-material solution at a stated ratio of 1:4, homogenized the mixtures, froze them at −80 °C and freeze-dried them for about 72 hours.[1] The MD:GA labels describe the carrier blend, not the composition of undiluted clove extract. The method does not specify the basis of the 1:4 ratio; it should not be read as a verified dry extract-to-carrier mass ratio.[1]

For initial water activity, the researchers used an analyzer at 25 °C.[1] For hygroscopicity, they exposed 1 g of powder to a saturated sodium chloride environment at 75.3% relative humidity and weighed it after seven days.[1] The latter method describes humid exposure, not testing of a sealed retail pouch. It does not state an exposure temperature or give an explicit calculation equation for the reported hygroscopicity percentage.[1]

The table below reproduces the water-activity and hygroscopicity columns from the original paper's Table 2. Values are means ± standard deviations; the study reports three separate experimental runs.[1]

The overall formulation comparison was nonsignificant for water activity (p = 0.17), but significant for hygroscopicity (p < 0.01).[1] In the hygroscopicity column, different letters denote differences under the authors' Tukey test; the four MD-rich formulations share the letter b.[1] Thus, 75:25 had the lowest numerical hygroscopicity, but the study does not establish it as significantly better than 62.5:37.5, 87.5:12.5 or all-MD on that measure. Nor does the nonsignificant water-activity result establish formal equivalence.

There are reporting inconsistencies worth retaining rather than smoothing over. Table 2 gives all-MD moisture as 1.39% and solubility as 93.3%, whereas the discussion gives 1.30% and 95%; the all-GA solubility of 89.9% also conflicts with the abstract's blanket “>90%” description.[1] Those disputed moisture and solubility values are not used in the comparison above.

If the purchasing objective includes clove aroma, ask for a relevant chemical result and an application sensory assessment separately. The clove study measured eugenol by HPLC and phenolics by chemical assays; those endpoints are not a sensory-panel measurement of aroma retention.[1] Its Table 4 gives eugenol loading efficiencies of 70.5–75.6%, with no significant formulation effect reported (p = 0.78).[1] Here, loading efficiency compares the measured eugenol concentration after drying with the theoretical concentration before drying; it is not the eugenol mass fraction of the powder.[1] That does not support declaring the lowest-uptake blend the best eugenol-retaining blend.

An independent spray-drying experiment offers another useful caution. It used 99%-purity eugenol—not whole clove extract—with a fixed MD:GA blend of 3:1 and added soy lecithin, while varying processing conditions and the eugenol-to-polymer ratio across 32 experiments.[3] Its Table 3 reports 96.07% eugenol encapsulation efficiency but only 33.72% product recovery for DF16; DF06 instead gave 47.37% efficiency and 65.35% recovery.[3] A high result on one endpoint did not identify the best overall manufacturing outcome.

The two papers also use “encapsulation efficiency” differently. The clove paper calculates (total core phenolics − surface phenolics) / total core phenolics × 100; the eugenol paper compares experimental with theoretical eugenol content.[1][3] Their percentages should not appear together in a carrier-performance ranking. The independent study helps separate processing yield from compound loading; it does not replicate the clove humidity experiment or establish sensory retention.

A separate study of spray-dried elderberry pomace extract illustrates the transfer problem. Its all-MD formulation had a reported moisture content of 5.63 ± 0.15%, compared with 4.10 ± 0.09% for all-GA—the reverse of the endpoint ordering in the freeze-dried clove study.[2][1] The elderberry experiment used a different extract and spray drying at an inlet temperature of 120 ± 1 °C.[2] Its methods contain an unresolved ratio discrepancy: the drying section states 1:2 carrier:extract dry mass, while the assay section uses 1:6 extract:carrier to calculate expected compound concentration.[2] The moisture results are cited as reported; neither ratio is used here to calculate a carrier fraction or normalize performance.

For an aroma-led application, add eugenol content and a sensory comparison in the intended formulation. For a sealed-pack project, test the actual powder–package combination against agreed end-of-life criteria. The clove paper separately tested storage in screw-capped tubes at 4 or 25 °C for 40 days and in sealed tubes at 60 °C for seven days.[1] Neither those storage tests nor the seven-day humidity exposure establish a pouch barrier requirement, a desiccant dose or a shelf life.[1]

研究人员先用80%甲醇提取丁香花蕾，将提取液浓缩、冻干，再进行包埋。[1] 壁材采用麦芽糊精（MD，葡萄糖当量16.5–19.5）与阿拉伯胶（GA）的六种配比，文中将冻干提取物与浓度为30% w/v的壁材溶液按1:4混合；混合物经过均质、−80 °C冷冻，再冻干约72小时。[1] MD:GA描述的是载体内部的配比，不是纯丁香提取物的组成。方法段没有交代1:4的计量基准，不能直接把它当作已确认的干提取物与载体质量比。[1]
初始水分活度在25 °C下用仪器测定。[1] 吸湿性则采用另一项试验：将1 g粉末置于饱和氯化钠溶液形成的75.3%相对湿度环境中，七天后称重。[1] 这是湿空气暴露试验，不是密封零售包装测试；该方法段没有明确给出暴露温度，也没有列出吸湿性百分数的计算公式。[1]
下表摘录原论文表2中的水分活度和吸湿性数据。数值为均值±标准差；作者报告分三次开展实验。[1]
配方间水分活度的总体比较未达到统计显著水平（p = 0.17），吸湿性的总体比较则显著（p < 0.01）。[1] 吸湿性一列中的不同字母表示作者采用Tukey检验得到的差异分组；麦芽糊精比例较高的四组均标为b。[1] 所以，75:25组虽然吸湿性数值最低，却不能据此说它显著优于62.5:37.5、87.5:12.5或全麦芽糊精组。同样，“水分活度差异不显著”也不等于已经完成等效性验证。
原论文还有几处数字不一致，需要保留说明。全麦芽糊精组的水分在表2中为1.39%，正文写成1.30%；溶解度在表中为93.3%，正文则为95%。全阿拉伯胶组溶解度89.9%，也与摘要笼统表述的“>90%”不符。[1] 上面的比较没有采用这些存在矛盾的水分和溶解度数字。

如果采购目的包括丁香香气，应把相关化学检测与实际应用中的感官评价分开提出。丁香研究使用HPLC测定丁香酚，并用化学方法测定酚类；这些结果不是感官评价人员对香气保留的评分。[1] 其表4中丁香酚的负载效率为70.5%–75.6%，报告的配方效应不显著（p = 0.78）。[1] 这里的负载效率是干燥后实测丁香酚浓度与干燥前理论浓度之比，不是粉末中丁香酚的质量分数。[1] 因此，不能据此把吸湿性最低的配方同时列为丁香酚保留最好的配方。
另一项独立的喷雾干燥研究提供了不同角度。该研究使用99%纯度的丁香酚，而不是完整丁香提取物；MD:GA固定为3:1，并加入大豆卵磷脂，在32组实验中改变加工条件及丁香酚与聚合物的比例。[3] 其表3显示，DF16的丁香酚包埋效率为96.07%，产品回收率却只有33.72%；DF06的相应结果则为47.37%和65.35%。[3] 单项指标很高，并不意味着制造过程的综合结果最好。
两篇论文的“包埋效率”也不能直接横比。丁香提取物研究按“（总核心酚−表面酚）/总核心酚×100”计算；丁香酚研究比较的是实际丁香酚含量与理论含量。[1][3] 把两组百分数放进同一张载体性能排行榜，会混淆测量对象和分母。独立研究有助于说明产品回收率与成分负载是不同目标，但它没有重复丁香粉末的吸湿试验，也没有验证感官上的留香表现。

另一项接骨木果渣提取物喷雾干燥研究，说明了跨原料套用结论的风险。它的全麦芽糊精组水分为5.63 ± 0.15%，全阿拉伯胶组为4.10 ± 0.09%，这两组的水分高低顺序与丁香冻干研究相反。[2][1] 接骨木研究使用的提取物不同，喷雾干燥进风温度为120 ± 1 °C。[2] 其方法段还存在未解决的比例矛盾：干燥部分写的是载体与提取物干物质之比1:2，检测部分却按提取物与载体之比1:6计算理论成分浓度。[2] 这里仅引用作者报告的水分结果，不采用任一比例推算载体含量，也不据此换算性能。
如果项目主要看重香气，就增加丁香酚含量检测，以及目标配方中的感官对比。如果项目使用密封包装，则应针对实际粉末与包装组合，按约定的货架期末验收指标开展试验。丁香论文还另行开展了储存试验：样品在旋盖管内于4或25 °C储存40天，或在密封管内于60 °C放置七天。[1] 这些储存试验与七天湿度暴露试验，都不能直接给出包装袋阻隔指标、干燥剂用量或保质期。[1]
